sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS CREDIT CARDS.  FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER MAKES USE OF CREDIT CARDS.  HOW DO THEY COMPARE TO YOUR OWN?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantB: Are you from the survey?
ParticipantA: Yeah, I got the call too. I'm just glad I'm not talking to an actual salesperson.
ParticipantB: Me too. My boss tried to upsell me on a rewards card last week, it was weird.
ParticipantA: Right. So, how are you?
ParticipantB: I'm good, just tired. Work is a bit stressful lately.
ParticipantA: Same here. You know, I think credit cards are mostly good for building credit, honestly.
ParticipantB: Really? I used to think that, but now I'm on the fence.
ParticipantA: Yeah, exactly. It's about the discipline, not the plastic itself.
ParticipantB: That makes sense. My husband actually had a financial meltdown five years ago.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's... that's really hard to hear. I didn't know that.
ParticipantB: Yeah, he maxed out three cards and couldn't pay them back. He lost his house.
ParticipantA: Wow. That's a dark side I never really considered. I guess I just never let it get that bad.
ParticipantB: Exactly. Since then, I only use my card for gas and groceries, and I pay it off every single month.
ParticipantA: That's actually what I do too. I pay it off in full.
ParticipantB: Really? That's unusual. Most people I know just swipe and forget.
ParticipantA: Well, I learned that lesson a long time ago. I think I made it up back when I was in my thirties, something about it just feeling safer that way.
ParticipantB: I see. That's a good point. You seem pretty comfortable with it then.
ParticipantA: Yeah, mostly. Though sometimes I get tempted to buy something expensive I don't need.
ParticipantB: Oh, totally. I feel that all the time. That's why I'm so careful now.
ParticipantA: Right, the temptation is the real enemy.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Does it bother you at all? Just knowing you carry the debt around?
ParticipantA: A little bit. Sometimes I worry about interest rates creeping up, but overall I'm fine with it.
ParticipantB: I'm glad to hear that. At least your experience is different from my friend's.
ParticipantA: It is. It's a fine line, I guess.
ParticipantB: True. A fine line between a useful tool and a dangerous weapon.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that sums it up nicely.
ParticipantB: Okay, well I think we've said enough. Thanks for chatting.
ParticipantA: Sure, no problem. Good luck with the survey.
ParticipantB: You too. Bye.
ParticipantA: Bye.
